full_judgment:
16. Since the present case has not been decided by the lower appellate Court solely on the concession of the lawyer of the plaintiff-respondents, but also partly on a partial consideration of the evidence on record, it now falls to be considered whether the lower appellate Court has properly reversed the relevant findings of the trial Court with regard to the property Nos. 2 and 4 of schedule 'Ka' and the property of schedule 'Kha'. A judgment of reversal need not allude to all the reasons given by the Court below and it can sustain itself if it is intrinsically cogent enough to stand on its own, but a judgment of reversal which does not discuss or allude to the salient and unavoidable ground or grounds on the basis of which the trial Court came to a contrary conclusion must be deemed to be vitiated by an error of procedure. 

 17. From are reading of the judgments of the two courts below it appears to be patent that the compelling reasons which prompted the trial Court to hold that all the land of all the schedules belonged to the four brothers were neither alluded to nor discussed by the lower appellate Court in coming to a contrary decision on facts. The judgment of the lower appellate Court therefore was not a proper judgment of reversal. The High Court Division did not correctly appreciate the nature of the judgment of the lower appellate Court. It was not a judgment based fully and exclusively on the concession of the lawyer of the plaintiff-respondents. It contains also a partial discussion of the evidence on record. Since this discussion is selective and does not meet the requirement of a judgment of reversal we hold that the judgment of the lower appellate Court cannot stand. Therefore, the impugned judgment of the High Court Division setting aside the same does not call for any interference for the reasons stated above which are somewhat different from those given in support of the said judgment. The decision was correct but not quite the reason.
